verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes DCDC1 as the 2A, 3.3V source for the normal-operation rail, defining concrete power-system behavior.
The client changes the programmed DCDC1 output from 3.3V to 3.4V to maintain a 3.3V downstream rail after the diode drop; the existing voltage key is replaced without requiring a removal.
This is the first concrete regulator failure: factory measurements show unstable L3 voltage on two boards, with later context resolving L3 to the DCDC1 path.
This adds distinct failure modes and paths: idle undervoltage, USB-powered transient collapse, intermittent register latching, and eventual complete DCDC1 degradation.
